subject.title: Feature request: Persistent task-status surface for long-running channel turns

question: Should OpenClaw add a persistent channel-turn status surface now, and should its canonical owner be the runtime/session layer, the task ledger, or the channel progress-draft transport?
rationale: The remaining work is not a small bug fix; it chooses user-visible terminal semantics, restart ownership, channel rollout, and how several existing status surfaces avoid becoming competing sources of truth.

options.title: Design a runtime-owned status contract
options.body: Create a generic run/session status owner first, then let Discord render it as a best-effort editable status message without making progress drafts or task records the source of truth.

options.title: Narrow to progress-draft enhancement
options.body: Treat the feature as Discord progress-draft UX only, accepting that unknown/interrupted durability remains out of scope until a later runtime state model exists.

options.title: Defer behind session activity work
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for the broader session activity API to define canonical run-state semantics before adding channel-visible status messages.

recommendation.title: Design a runtime-owned status contract
recommendation.body: Create a generic run/session status owner first, then let Discord render it as a best-effort editable status message without making progress drafts or task records the source of truth.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest adjacent history is in progress drafts, Discord preview transport, and channel streaming surfaces, while the decision still needs coordination with task/status owners.
